paragraphs.text: Turkish (Türkçe) language pack for the DeepSeek Harness Web UI — 64 namespaces, 2,910 strings, MIT
# dsh-turkish-locale

Turkish (**Türkçe**) language pack for the DeepSeek Harness
Web UI. A community plugin built on the

documented client-plugin locale API —
no changes to the packaged application, no rebuild.
## What it does

- Registers `tr` with an `en` fallback through `ctx.locale.addLanguage` and
`ctx.locale.register`.
-

Translates **73 namespaces / 3,838 strings** — 100% of the English UI copy
shipped in DSH **0.2.2-r

c.1** (commit `c59d10a`; v1.1.0). Placeholders,
Markdown, separator strings and punctuation are pres

erved and validated
against source.
- The language appears in **Settings → General → Language → Türk

çe**; the choice
persists as `locale.preference` in `cordis.patch.yml`, `<html lang>` follows the
ac
tive locale, and English/Turkish switching works live in both directions.
## Install

The package is both a client plugin and a DSH **bundle** (`dsh.bundle.patch`), so
it can be installe
d manually or from a plugin market index.
### From the DSH plugin market (Discover)
Market index:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

Add that URL as an index source in **Plugins → More → Discover** (Settings →
Plugins also lists the

configured sources), then install "Türkçe dil paketi".
The installer pins
`git+https://github.com/mk

feyman/dsh-turkish-locale#<commit>`, so **Git** must be
available to pnpm on the machine.
### Manual install
1. Copy this package into a DSH profile's `node_modules`:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
2. Add rows to the profile's `cordis.patch.yml`:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

3. With HMR enabled the pack activates in the running app; otherwise restart the
app (or reload the
Web GUI). Choose **Ayarlar → Genel → Dil** to switch.
## Compatibility

- Verified working on **DSH 0.2.2-rc.1** (commit `c59d10a`): the pack loads from
the boot graph, the

selector lists 8 built-in languages plus Türkçe, switching
round-trips, and `locale.preference: tr`

persists. Runtime contracts
(`addLanguage`, `register(ns, locale, dict)`, `resolveText`, snapshot)

are
unchanged from 0.2.1-rc.3. See
`docs/upgrade-analysis-0.2.2-rc1.md`.
- **Coverage (v1.1.0):** re

-extracted from 0.2.2-rc.1 and translated to
**73 namespaces / 3,838 strings — 100 %** of the shippe

d English UI copy,
including the 981 strings added by 0.2.2 (10 new namespaces:
`forgePanel` 253, `l

iveshare` 225, `stats` 177, …). The 60 changed English
source values were reviewed and updated where

the meaning moved. Measured
delta and fixture notes: `fixtures/version-coverage.json`.
Release note
s: `docs/release-notes-v1.1.0.md`.
## Repository layout
| Path | Purpose |

| `lib/client.js` | Browser bundle registering the language and dictionaries |
| `lib/index.js` | Em

pty host half (Loader row) |
| `cordis.patch.yml` | Bundle patch: adds the `tr-locale` row and defau

lts the locale to `tr` |
| `locales/tr.json` | Full namespace → key → Turkish dictionary data |
| `m

arket-index.json` | Plugin market index listing this bundle (format 1) |
| `fixtures/` | Determinist

ic 59.4 % Turkish subset + expected ordered-lookup samples |
| `patches/` | Draft patch for ordered

locale preference (#11699) |
| `locale/` | Package-localized title/description |
| `docs/` | Screens
hots and market icon |
## Ordered locale preference (Discussion #11699)

The community proposal to replace the single UI locale with an ordered
preference list (`ru → en → z
h`) is supported by this pack. We published:

- **Patch draft** for `packages/client/locale`, rebased to **`dsh-v0.2.2-rc.1`**
(tag commit `66491b

05…`) and **CI-validated**:
`patches/0003-ordered-locale-preference-0.2.2-rc1.patch`
(17 files: the

locale package — legacy `string` preferences read as
one-element lists, `snapshot.active` stays the

first entry, lookup expands each
preferred language's fallback chain and ends at English, reorderabl

e settings
row — plus 5 sibling test fixtures whose `LocaleSnapshot` literals gain
`preference`). Ap

plied to a checked-out rc.1 tree: **vitest 79/79**, sanctioned
typecheck gate **5/5**, patch self-ch

eck reproduces the tree exactly — see
`patches/validation-report-0.2.2-rc1.json`.
Older variants: `0

002`
(alpha.2) and `0001` (rc.3).
- **Fixture** to exercise it: `fixtures/` — a 59.4 %
Turkish subse

t (1728 / 2910 keys) plus `expected-behavior.json` samples for
`["tr","en"]`, `["en","tr"]`, `["tr",

"zh"]` and the legacy single selection;
`version-coverage.json` records why the 0.2.2 delta (9 names

paces / 853 strings)
falls through to English in fixture tests.
- **Layer-2 audit:** `tools/audit_lo

cale_gaps.py`
measures the case ordering cannot fix — namespaces that register only `zh` and
CJK key

s that would leak as raw text — from a local dictionary dump
(`{namespace: {locale: {key: value}}}`)

. Sample: `fixtures/audit-sample.json`.
Classification confirmed with `@ragnoryok1`: typed (zh+en) d

ictionaries are
fixed by ordering; per-locale `zh`-only dictionaries are not, and a tarball
listing

cannot distinguish them, so the rule belongs at registration time.
- **Live demo:** the fixture was

installed as a temporary `tr-partial` language
pack and selected in Settings → General → Language, r

endering a mixed
Turkish/English UI (screenshot below). The demo pack was removed afterwards.

The Turkish pack is unaffected by the change: `tr → en` behaves exactly like the
ordered list `["tr"

ish pack is unaffected by the change: `tr → en` behaves exactly like the
ordered list `["tr","en"]`.
## Provenance

The dictionaries were extracted from the English source of the client packages
installed with DSH 0.

2.1-rc.3 and translated namespace by namespace; every
translated value was checked against its sourc

e placeholder set before the
bundle was generated. The proposal was shared with the DeepSeek Harness

team in
Discussions #11015.
## License
MIT — see LICENSE.
